item.title: Comment on Why northern England is poor by PK
item.description:
Having moved from US to UK, I find the English centralisation of power to tax, spend, and set policy mind-boggling.

At one stage, we had the central cabinet decide on planning permission for a building. We had the central Minister veto a plan to build 350 flats in a London suburb.

Local mayors have little to no ability to raises taxes and make local spending decisions. Most taxes are collected and shipped off to Westminster to be sent back, with strings attached.

This centralisation particularly affects the North. Due to agglomeration effects built up over centuries, the ROI of any new infra investment in London is 10x, so it keeps growing. Infra funding is scare, because we love to waste and over-engineer everything, so it keeps coming down to London vs. North, and London keeps winning.

Sam Freedman's book Failed State outlines the dysfunction.
